title: Select the date and the 30-minute downtime window for the cutover
summary: The cutover needs a 30-minute window with low traffic. The plan recommends Sunday 10 January 2027, 02:00–02:30, after the peak freeze, so the rollback window does not overlap the peak.

badges.tip: Only you can accept the downtime and the date.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: With CDC (D1 option b), the shop is closed for about 15 minutes. The window adds 15 minutes of buffer for the smoke tests and a rollback start. The date must leave time to close F5 and F6 first.

blocks.title: What we found
blocks.html:
• [READ] The peak freeze runs from 20 November 2026 to 4 January 2027. No production changes are allowed in it. [src: report.md]
  • [READ] Sunday 02:00–02:30 has the lowest traffic: 41 orders per minute. Tuesday 03:00–03:30 has 57. [src: report.md]
  • [INFERRED] The work for the move is 31 engineer-days. With 2 engineers, that is about 16 working days. [src: report.md]

blocks.title: If you change D1
blocks.html: If you select D1 option a, the window must be about 9 hours long. Then only a Sunday night from 00:00 to 09:00 is possible.

options.label: Sunday 15 November 2026, 02:00–02:30
options.detail_html: Effect: the savings start 2 months earlier (about $5,400). Risk: high. The plan has no slack. The ORM release (F5) gets less than one week on MySQL. The 7-day rollback window ends on 22 November, after the peak freeze starts.

options.label: Sunday 10 January 2027, 02:00–02:30
options.detail_html: Effect: about 6 weeks of slack after the staging work. Traffic is 41 orders per minute. Cost: about $5,400 of savings come later. Risk: low.

options.label: Tuesday 12 January 2027, 03:00–03:30
options.detail_html: Effect: a working day, so the full team is at work the next morning. Traffic is 57 orders per minute, about 1.4 times the Sunday rate. Cost: the same as option b.

recommendation_html: Option b. The rollback window and the peak freeze do not overlap. The plan also gets time to close F5 and F6 before the cutover. The cost is a delay of savings, not new spending.
